rationale:
Crosses the render-assets-and-backends watch family only through its broad `core/view/**` selector, the same way 20260912-overlay-dismissal-single-policy-watch did. Every source file in this change is under core/view: core/view/src/widget_bridge.cpp, core/view/src/pointer_dispatch.cpp, and core/view/{src,include/pulp/view}/context_menu.{cpp,hpp}. Nothing under core/canvas or core/render is touched, no Skia, Dawn, or render-backend selector is crossed, no design-system asset changes, and no packaging or asset-resolution behaviour changes.

The change makes a right-click reach its handler. A React onContextMenu prop had never worked in any Pulp app: prop-applier lowercases the prop name and emits on(id, 'contextmenu', cb), and the on() preamble in widget_bridge.cpp routed click, hover, pointer, gesture and wheel to __ensureNativeRegistered__ while dropping contextmenu, so registerContextMenu was never issued and View::on_context_menu stayed null. Separately, dispatch_context_menu fired only the hit-tested view's callback with no target-to-root walk, so a listener on a wrapper never ran when the press landed on a child canvas drawn over it -- which is how contextmenu behaves in the DOM and how real pages are built. Both halves were required; fixing either alone still produces nothing on such a tree. The registered callback is also corrected from a call expression to a function expression, which is what event_api.cpp's `cb + "(" + x + "," + y + ")"` composition requires: the old form dispatched with a literal 0 where the event belongs, discarding the press coordinates, and then threw a TypeError that safe_dispatch_eval swallowed.

ContextMenu additionally gains accepts_navigation_input() while open -- both macOS hosts gate navigation keys on that predicate, so its existing arrow-key handling was unreachable in a plugin editor or standalone -- plus Home/End. Wrapping at the ends is deliberately not added, because test_context_menu.cpp asserts the clamp with a stated rationale.

No rendering, paint, layout, or asset behaviour changes; no bridge function is removed or re-signatured and both dispatch_context_menu overloads keep their declarations; no generated artifact or manifest row moves. Registered watch-only so the family's coverage stays honest about a change that crossed its selector. No authority moves, no accepted expansion boundary moves, and no Vellum artifact changes.
